problem: OVMM systems usually navigate to a location merely near the target using geometric planners (A*, RRT*), ignoring affordances, so manipulation often fails (wrong side of cabinet, pot handle misaligned). VLM-only methods reason on a single egocentric RGB image and ignore geometric feasibility and reachability.
motivation: Base placement is critical for manipulation success and requires joint reasoning about semantic intent (which side/part to face) and geometric feasibility (clearance, reach), often beyond the camera's narrow field of view. VLMs are semantically strong but poorly grounded spatially, so an explicit link between RGB semantics and a top-down map is needed.
key_idea: Project VLM-derived affordance directions onto both the RGB image and the obstacle map (Affordance RGB + Obstacle Map+), then run a zero-shot iterative sampling and VLM-ranking optimization whose weight shifts from semantic to geometric scoring (coarse-to-fine).
insight: VLMs cannot reliably turn RGB semantic understanding into spatially grounded map reasoning on their own. Removing the projection drops success from 85% to 48%, and removing main arrow 'A' drops it to 62%. Fixed weightings of semantics and geometry fail: alpha=0 gives 43%, alpha=0.5 gives 76%, alpha=1 gives 79%, versus 85% for the increasing alpha_t schedule, because semantics-first sampling finds the right region and geometry-later ensures reachability.
method: Pipeline: GPT-4 parses the instruction into (object, sub-task) tuples; the robot navigates by A* to within 1.5 m of the object, selects a base placement, then executes a predefined manipulation primitive. Object 2D position and the global map are given by the simulator.

Affordance Guidance Projection: Grounded SAM segments the target and back-projects depth onto the obstacle map to get a footprint and centroid. 12 colored arrows at 30° spacing are rendered in both the RGB and the map. GPT-4o picks the affordance direction by 3-vote majority, which is marked 'A' and yields a ±60° fan-shaped region.
Affordance RGB and Obstacle Map+: two color-consistent cross-modal inputs to the VLM. The RGB carries arrows and 'A'; the map carries the object footprint, robot position, fan region and arrows.

Affordance point selection (ReKep-like): DINOv2 features inside the Grounded SAM mask are clustered by k-means (k=20, cosine), keypoints are pruned at 0.08 m, and GPT-4o picks the one matching the sub-task, giving the sampling center g.

Iterative sampling and scoring: candidates come from a truncated Gaussian around g (N=1000, r_max=1.2 m, collision-free with ≥0.4 m clearance). Score w=w_geo^alpha_t · w_sem^(1-alpha_t), where w_geo favors a preferred radius r*=0.7 m and w_sem favors proximity to the semantic center mu_t. alpha_t follows a sigmoid schedule with alpha_max=0.6.

VLM ranking and refinement: 20 resampled candidates are indexed on Obstacle Map+ and GPT-4o returns the top-3. mu_t is their mean and sigma_s decays over T=4 iterations. At the final iteration the top-5 are taken, the 2 furthest from their mean are dropped, and the other 3 are averaged as the base placement.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) for direction, keypoint and candidate ranking; GPT-4 for instruction parsing; Grounded SAM; DINOv2
setting.observation: head-mounted RGB-D (1280x720) with known intrinsics/extrinsics, 2D occupancy grid map (200x200, 0.05 m/cell), language instruction
setting.action_space: selected 2D base placement (x,y) on the map, reached with A* navigation; predefined manipulation primitives (pick, place, open) via IK
setting.privileged: GT 2D target object position from the simulator and a known global obstacle map

numbers.eval_set_note: 5 custom tasks x 20 randomized trials each (100 total)
numbers.extra: GT object 2D position and global obstacle map given; predefined manipulation primitives

numbers_note: Custom benchmark with no standard name and no official split, so 'test' is a placeholder; per-task rates are converted from k/20 counts. Ablation numbers (alpha and projection) are in the results text; the projection ablation is a figure with values given in the caption.
results: The method reaches 85% overall success across five tasks (20 trials each), versus 61% for the best geometric baseline (Affordance Point + RRT*), 50% for Object Center + RRT*, and 26% / 23% for the PIVOT variants. The alpha ablation (43/76/79% for fixed values) and projection ablation (80/62/48%) support both the coarse-to-fine schedule and the cross-modal projection.
limitations: Placements can have limited geometric precision, especially for distance estimation, and VLM reasoning can still be wrong.
The arm may collide during execution in cluttered spaces because arm trajectory feasibility is not part of the optimization.
Evaluated only in simulation on 5 tasks with GT object position and a known map, with no real-robot test; needs many VLM calls per placement.
